title: Recover a responsive vertical slice

bridge.applicationConcept: Responsive layout, component state, wrapping, and overflow
bridge.analogyLimit: A viewport is not a network link; content priority and human comprehension matter more than raw fitting capacity.

buildBrief: Implement the approved ClearPath service section as a responsive Next.js component with semantic structure, reusable props, and explicit loading-independent content.
incidentBrief: A fixed minimum width and non-wrapping action row cause horizontal overflow. Use browser evidence to identify the owning rule and repair it without redesigning the section.

scenario.symptoms: The 320-pixel viewport test reports horizontal overflow and a clipped secondary action.

acceptanceTests: The vertical slice matches the approved content hierarchy
No horizontal overflow occurs from 320 pixels through desktop widths
The learner identifies the exact component and CSS rule responsible
predictionQuestions: Which element do you expect to define the minimum page width?
Will wrapping, shrinking, or clipping best preserve content priority?
defenseQuestions: Trace props into rendered semantic HTML and styles.
Explain why the failing rule affected the whole page.
Change one breakpoint behavior without rewriting the component.
hints: Find the widest element before editing media queries.
Inspect min-width, white-space, flex-wrap, and child shrink behavior.
Prefer a layout rule that works across widths over a single device patch.
